author: Darlene Prois
title: Seeley Lions Pre-Fat: A local treasure - NewsBreak
text: No matter your age or ability, if you can pedal a bike, you can ride in The Seeley Lions PreFat Mountain Bike Race. As many as 300 participants are expected for this local favorite on Saturday, August 23. For the first time, riders of pedal assist e-bikes are invited to race in any of the four events, and for riders under 10, the popular (and free!) Cub Race returns. Mountain bike races have increased exponentially in the past decade, but the Seeley Lions PreFat Mountain Bike Race endures, thanks to its intensely local focus and community support. Participation has remained steady since this classic race began in 1996. Winding through gravel, forest roads and single track in the famed Chequamegon National Forest, the race has become an accessible draw for the whole family, Four separate races provide challenges for beginning to expert riders. Distances range from 10 miles, with a Junior Division for riders aged 10-17 and Senior divisions for ages 17 and up; the 17-mile Sport Division for riders aged 12 and older and the 25-mile Expert Division for riders aged 16 and older. Riders under 10 may participate in the free Cub Race, held after other competitors have finished. The majority of riders typically come from Wisconsin or Minnesota. In the past several years, the race has become a testing ground for the Hayward Mountain Bike Team, attracting riders in sixth through twelfth grade. For many young riders, it is their first racing experience. For more experienced riders, the CAMBA single track sections of the Sport and Expert courses test rider skills, whether racing by Lake Helene or taking on the challenging Flow Mama, Gravity Cavity, and Martel’s Pot Hole. Class 1 pedal-assist e-bikes are allowed in all events, but are not eligible for prizes. Each race starts with a controlled rollout, and finishes in the same open area at the Kortoloppet start at the Birkie OO trailhead. A picnic-style lunch featuring Louie’s Birkie Brats and beverages is free to participants and available for purchase to bystanders. The course starts and finishes at the Kortelopet start area near the Birkie OO trailhead. The PreFat Race is the largest annual fundraiser for the Seeley Lions. Proceeds fund activities, projects, and assistance to local communities, including financial donations to non-profit organizations, food pantries, shelters and families in need. The club’s signature local projects include major improvements at Silverthorn Park, such as pickleball courts and changing rooms. The group is responsible for building a beautiful warming cabin for the Seeley Hills Recreational Area and also provides funding for trail management. Scholarships for area high school students are awarded each spring. Local sponsors are key to the race’s longevity. The PreFat is made possible thanks to generous sponsors, including Presenting Sponsor Freewheel Bikes and food and beverage sponsors Louie’s Finer Meats and Bent Paddle Brewing Company. Major sponsors include Sawmill Saloon, Norvado Communications, Tamarack Health, ROAM Basecamp, New Moon Ski and Bike, Riverbrook Bike and Ski, Sawyer County Record, Northern Lakes True Value Hardware, Pat Nelson Captioning LLC, Jersey Mike’s Subs, Cable Chamber of Commerce, Bakke Norman Law Office, Start Line Inn and the American Birkebeiner Ski Foundation. In addition, more than two dozen other local businesses contribute to the event. More information about the PreFat event and the work they do is available at SeeleyLions.org.
